title: In Weariness and Pain
description: In Weariness and Pain in Tonic Solfa to ST. BRIDE, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 504.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. BRIDE; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: In wea-ri-ness and pain, By sins and fears op-prest, I turn me to my Rest a-gain, My soul’s e-ter-nal Rest.

lines: I turn me to my Rest again,
The Lamb that died for me
And still my load doth bear;
To Jesus’ streaming wounds I flee
Thy sorrow, Lord, is my relief,
O may I rise with Thee

licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to ST. BRIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
